## (2) Approaches message

No implicit dependency was recorded as missing or not checkable. The traces of `jobs/report.ts` and `jobs/digest.ts` into `lib/notify.ts` found no loader, config, or runtime dependency beyond the shared helper itself. All three approaches move the report job onto the shared helper and delete its inline copy. They differ on one axis: how the channel enters the helper's contract, and therefore how many callers must change.

**Recommended: optional channel argument on `post` (reuse-only).** `post(message, channel = "general")` builds its body from the parameter instead of the literal. `report` becomes a one-line delegation: `post(message, channel)`. Formatting and the retry loop stay in exactly one place. The digest job keeps its call unchanged and still posts to `general`, so the blast radius is just the helper plus the report job. The trade-off is that the default remains implicit at every call that omits it. That is today's behavior, and you said a backward-compatible optional argument is allowed.

Adds: an optional `channel` parameter (default `"general"`) on `lib/notify.ts#post`; `jobs/report.ts#report` delegates to `post(message, channel)`; tests for the default channel, an explicit channel, and retry-then-throw in the notify test file
Pattern: follows the owning helper at lib/notify.ts:1-7 and extends it with a discriminant rather than a parallel path. It removes the duplicated copy at jobs/report.ts:2-6, which is the debt here.

**Required channel argument on `post`.** The signature becomes `post(message, channel)` with no default. `digest` changes to `post("Daily digest", "general")` and `report` delegates as above. Every destination becomes explicit at the call site, so no caller silently lands in `general`. The cost is caller blast radius. Every existing `post` call must be edited in the same change, and any caller outside the traced paths breaks at compile time. Within the traced code, that means one extra edit, at jobs/digest.ts:2. It meets every recorded requirement but changes more files for the same outcome.
Removes: the inline body and retry loop in `jobs/report.ts` (lines 2-6); the hard-coded `"general"` literal in `lib/notify.ts`
Adds: a required `channel` parameter on `lib/notify.ts#post`; an explicit `"general"` argument at jobs/digest.ts:2; `report` delegation; the same tests as above
Pattern: follows the owning helper at lib/notify.ts:1-7. It trades the implicit default for explicitness at every caller.

**Sibling export `postTo(channel, message)`, with `post` delegating.** This option drops the ask's assumption that `post`'s own signature has to change. `postTo` takes over the body and retry loop. `post(message)` becomes `postTo("general", message)` and `report` calls `postTo`. Existing callers see no signature change at all. The cost is two public entrypoints into one behavior, which leaves future callers a naming choice that the optional argument avoids.
Removes: the inline body and retry loop in `jobs/report.ts` (lines 2-6)
Adds: a `postTo(channel, message)` export in `lib/notify.ts`; `post` reduced to a delegating wrapper; `report` delegation; tests for `postTo` plus `post`'s default
Pattern: keeps a single implementation at lib/notify.ts but widens its public surface with a second entrypoint for one caller.

A no-change option is not viable. The only existing path that reaches a non-`general` channel is the inline copy at jobs/report.ts:2-6, which is the duplication this work removes.

I'd go with the optional argument: it delivers the report channel, keeps retries in one place, and touches no other caller. That flips to the required argument if you would rather have every call site name its destination than rely on a default, accepting the edit at jobs/digest.ts:2 and any compile breaks in untraced callers.

## 1. First message to the user

The framing holds: the supplied `lib/notify.ts#post`, `jobs/report.ts`, and `jobs/digest.ts` show the shared formatting and retry contract, the report job’s duplicate implementation, and the digest’s reliance on the default channel.

The fixtures support extending the shared helper: both implementations prefix messages with `[notice]`, attempt delivery twice, and rethrow the final failure. The helper currently hardcodes `general`; the report job already accepts a requested channel. The supplied traces found no additional loader or runtime dependency, and no load-bearing premise remains unverified.

Your recorded answers keep this framing and allow either an optional channel argument or a required argument with explicit defaults at existing callers. A new notification service is unnecessary. The design must preserve report channel selection, notification retries, and the digest’s delivery to `general`.

## 2. Approaches message

I recommend **A: extend the existing helper with an optional channel argument**. The distinction between these approaches is where the default-channel policy lives: inside the helper or explicitly at every caller. Neither requires a new service or a parallel notification path.

**A) Optional channel argument, defaulting to `general`**

Change the helper to `post(message: string, channel: string = "general")`, use that channel in its existing payload, and have `report(message, channel)` delegate to it. Leave `digest()` unchanged.

This is the minimal reuse-only option. The nearly-fitting path is `lib/notify.ts#post`; its only missing behavior is accepting a caller-selected channel. Formatting, two-attempt retries, and final-error propagation stay in their existing owner. Existing one-argument callers retain both their call shape and default-channel behavior. The trade-off is that callers can omit channel selection implicitly.

Removes: the inline payload construction, fetch call, and retry loop from `jobs/report.ts`.
Adds: a defaulted channel parameter and channel payload substitution in `lib/notify.ts#post`; a helper import and delegating call in `jobs/report.ts`.
Pattern: consolidates duplicated behavior into its existing owner, `lib/notify.ts#post`, while preserving the default-channel contract used by `jobs/digest.ts`.

**B) Required channel argument, with explicit defaults at callers**

Change the helper to `post(message: string, channel: string)`, delegate report delivery to it, and update the digest to call `post("Daily digest", "general")`.

This drops the assumption that existing calls must remain syntactically unchanged, as your recorded answer permits. It retains the shared implementation and makes destination selection visible at every call site. The cost is a broader caller migration: the digest must change despite needing no behavioral change, and any additional callers would require the same update.

Removes: the inline payload construction, fetch call, and retry loop from `jobs/report.ts`; the helper’s implicit default-channel policy.
Adds: a required channel parameter and channel payload substitution in `lib/notify.ts#post`; a helper import and delegating call in `jobs/report.ts`; an explicit `"general"` argument in `jobs/digest.ts`.
Pattern: retains centralized formatting and retry ownership in `lib/notify.ts#post`, but replaces the one-argument calling contract demonstrated by `jobs/digest.ts` with explicit destination selection.

I would switch the recommendation to **B** if requiring every caller to consciously select a destination became a requirement; otherwise **A** delivers the requested behavior with less caller disruption.
